findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data – no-op
findings.body: The new call `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` passes an empty object as `data`. Prisma's `updateMany` only updates fields explicitly listed in `data`, so with `{}` no columns (including the Prisma-managed `updatedAt`) are touched. The preceding comment "Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars under this credential" is therefore wrong – the call is a silent no-op. Either pass `updatedAt: new Date()` (or similar) to actually achieve the documented effect, or remove the call entirely. Note also that the PR description indicates `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is only updated by the webhook handler and is not displayed in the UI, so this added line is likely dead code that obscures the actual cache-refresh flow.

findings.title: macOS-only sed in-place edit breaks on Linux
findings.body: Line 68 uses `sed -i '' -E ...`. The `''` after `-i` is BSD/macOS syntax (sed takes a mandatory backup-suffix argument, with empty meaning no backup). On GNU sed (Linux/CI containers), `-i` does not take an argument and the script becomes `sed: invalid option -- 'E'` / treats `''` as the script. The PR's CI runs on Linux, so the script will fail on a fresh checkout. Use `sed -i.bak` followed by `rm *.bak`, or branch on the platform (e.g., `[[ "$OSTYPE" == darwin* ]] && SED_INPLACE="sed -i ''" || SED_INPLACE="sed -i"`).

findings.title: DropdownItem nested inside DropdownMenuItem produces invalid nested-button markup
findings.body: Both "Delete cached data" and "Remove App" actions are written as `<DropdownMenuItem><DropdownItem .../></DropdownMenuItem>`. Since `DropdownMenuItem` (Radix) is itself an interactive `<button>`/menuitem, and `DropdownItem` is a styled `<button>` from the same dropdown module, the rendered DOM becomes a button-in-button (invalid HTML, screen-reader/AT issues) and creates competing onClick handlers with confusing focus/hover states. Typically cal.com uses either DropdownMenuItem with text, OR DropdownItem (without the wrapping DropdownMenuItem) for styled actions. Remove the wrapping `DropdownMenuItem` around `DropdownItem` (or replace DropdownItem with plain text/icon inside the item) so that exactly one button is rendered per row.

findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars – stale cache status remains in UI
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` only fires a toast and the optional `onSuccess?.()` callback. Unlike `disconnectMutation` further down (which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`), `deleteCacheMutation` does not call `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. The platform-atom wrapper passes `onChanged` as the `onSuccess`, which is a consumer-defined callback that is not guaranteed to refetch the tRPC query. After a successful cache deletion the user will continue to see the previous "Last updated: <timestamp>" under "Cache Status" until a full page reload, even though the underlying rows are gone. Add an `onSettled` (or `onSuccess`) that invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` to match the disconnect flow.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt – reports status for expired cache rows
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` runs `groupBy` over `CalendarCache` with no `expiresAt` filter, so a credential whose only cache rows are past `expiresAt` still returns a row and the UI then renders a "Last updated: <old timestamp>" plus a "Delete cached data" entry. In contrast, `getCachedAvailability` correctly filters `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }`, so the user is told the cache exists/is recent even though no actual cache hit will ever occur. Add an `expiresAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now()) }` clause (or filter post-groupBy) so the displayed "Last updated" matches what `getCachedAvailability` would consider usable.

findings.title: Authorization failure throws generic Error – not a TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential isn't owned by the caller, the handler throws a plain `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. This surfaces as an opaque `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` over tRPC, gives the client the same status as a true server bug, and merges the two failure modes (not-found vs forbidden) into one message. Use `throw new TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "Credential not found or access denied" })` (or `NOT_FOUND` after a `findUnique`). That also makes the existing "Error deleting cache" toast in `CredentialActionsDropdown` distinguishable from genuine infrastructure failures if more granular handling is added later.

findings.title: Stale generated warning comment contradicts the migration body
findings.body: Prisma's autogenerated warning still claims: "Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty." The actual SQL adds `DEFAULT NOW()`, so the table *is* populated safely for existing rows. Leaving the contradictory header in place is confusing for future migrations/maintenance and for anyone reading the migration file. Either drop the Prisma warning block (since the developer manually fixed it) or replace it with a short comment explaining why a `DEFAULT NOW()` was used instead of `@updatedAt` for legacy rows.

findings.title: New deleteCache tRPC mutation and handler have no tests
findings.body: This PR adds a brand-new destructive tRPC route (`viewer.calendars.deleteCache`) along with its handler, plus two new repository methods (`getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, `updateManyByCredentialId`) and a new UI component (`CredentialActionsDropdown`). None of these have accompanying unit/integration tests. The handler in particular performs authorization (verifying the credential belongs to the calling user) and a destructive DB op (`calendarCache.deleteMany`), and is exactly the kind of cross-cutting call most worth covering. Please add tests for: (a) another user cannot delete your cache (authorization), (b) missing/invalid credentialId is rejected by zod, (c) `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` excludes expired entries (after the fix above) and groups multiple cache rows per credential correctly, and (d) `CredentialActionsDropdown` calls `connectedCalendars.invalidate` after a successful delete (after the fix above).
